label: SYNTHETIC known-answer test of the evaluation and selection stage (positive and negative controls). The junction, its demand, its signal plans and every candidate are written in code; no proposer runs (Muse is not exercised), so this is not a test of discovery. It says nothing about the real NGSIM Lankershim intersection 2 baseline, or about any real junction.

skipped: I7: the timing is the same as the baseline

what_is_tested: the evaluation and selection stage: the deterministic validator, paired SUMO runs, eligibility, paired comparisons, Holm's correction and the selection rule, on candidates whose answer is known in advance
what_is_not_tested: discovery: no proposer runs and Muse is not exercised; the correction is the pre-registered answer itself, written by code
purpose: To separate 'does the evaluation and selection stage confirm and select a known Pareto improvement' from 'the selection rule refuses trade-offs'. The bad plan already has Webster's split, but its cycle is far longer than the demand needs. The correction (Webster's optimum cycle and split) shortens every approach's red time, so by first principles it should improve every approach. Same negative controls.
design_history: Designed on 2026-10-29 AFTER seeing the reallocation scenario's result. There, the stage confirmed the Webster split correction's improvements, the largest of any candidate, but the selection rule refused it because the N-S queues worsened: a trade-off, which the rule refuses by design. This scenario tests whether the stage selects a known improvement that involves no such trade-off. Its design and pre-registration were fixed before any simulation of it and were not tuned after its simulation output. Revised on 2026-10-29 after an independent review: framed as a test of the evaluation and selection stage, not of discovery; an exact null and the mirror of the correction added as negative controls; provenance from git. The design numbers are unchanged.

design.movements: through only: N->S, E->W, S->N, W->E; one approach lane per arm

expectation.kind: assumed (analytical; computed from the design only, before any simulation)
expectation.method: Webster (1958) optimum cycle and split; clearances unchanged

formula.flow_ratio: y_i = max over the approaches served in phase i of q_a / (n_lanes_a * s)
formula.optimum_cycle: C0 = (1.5 L + 5) / (1 - Y), with Y = sum_i y_i
formula.displayed_green: G_i = g_i - I + l (with l = I, as assumed here, G_i = g_i)
formula.whole_seconds: largest remainder, keeping sum_i G_i = C - n_phases * I; a phase below the minimum green gets the minimum and the others share the rest in proportion
formula.delay_for_predictions_only: Webster (1958): d = C(1-lam)^2 / (2(1-lam*x)) + x^2/(2q(1-x)) - 0.65 (C/q^2)^(1/3) x^(2+5 lam), lam = G/C, x = q/(s*lam), q and s in veh/s
formula.queues_for_predictions_only: mean queue (veh) = q*d (Little's law); queue at the end of red (veh) = q*r with red r = C - G

assumptions: saturation flow s = 1800 veh/h per lane (textbook base value, not calibrated against SUMO). Every approach has the same lanes, so s cancels out of the split; it matters for the optimum cycle and the degrees of saturation (see sensitivity)
lost time per phase l = 5 s, equal to the intergreen (yellow 3 s + all-red 2 s): start-up loss and use of the yellow assumed to cancel, so effective green = displayed green
cycle: Webster's C0 rounded up to whole seconds (the conservative side of its flat optimum), moved into the validator's 30-180 s if outside
yellow, all-red and phase order unchanged
through movements only; no turning, pedestrian or lane-utilisation factors

cycle.method: Webster's optimum cycle rounded up to whole seconds, within the validator's cycle limits

mirror.rule: 2 * bad - correction; if outside the validator's limits, scaled down to the maximum green and cycle keeping the split, then whole seconds with the minimum green

baseline.kind: simulated (validity checks only; program and demand are assumed)

limitations: SYNTHETIC known-answer test of the evaluation and selection stage (positive and negative controls). The junction, its demand, its signal plans and every candidate are written in code; no proposer runs (Muse is not exercised), so this is not a test of discovery. It says nothing about the real NGSIM Lankershim intersection 2 baseline, or about any real junction.

Report text written for counted demand does not apply to this designed demand: the clip length ('Counts come from a 3600 s clip; flow intervals are wide'), the note on stop-line discharge counts, and the Poisson 95% flow interval shown for each movement describe counting vehicles in a clip. Here the flows are designed, so those intervals carry no information.
The bundle's instruction to a model ('state expected effects in words, not numbers') does not apply: no model was asked; every candidate was written by code from the pre-registration.
The analytical Webster model is not calibrated against SUMO (saturation flow assumed); it only labels expected directions.
The small random perturbations change a deliberately bad plan by up to 5 s per green; they are not nulls. The exact null is rejected by the validator before simulation, so no simulated null exists.
This scenario was designed after seeing the reallocation result.

In the baseline the queue was censored on arm N (vehicles held off at entry on seed 6), arm E (a lane filled on seeds 2, 8; vehicles held off at entry on seeds 1, 2, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 13, 16, 17), arm S (vehicles held off at entry on seeds 1, 2), arm W (vehicles held off at entry on seeds 4, 13, 19), so those arms' queue claims are untestable for every candidate (lower bounds).

false_positives.opportunities_definition: tested improvement claims (p-value computed) whose predicted change is > 0: the claims that would be false positives if confirmed
false_positives.rule_of_three_note: 3/n when 0 of n; it treats the claims as independent, which they are not (they share the baseline runs)

model_agreement.note: verdicts against an uncalibrated Webster model (assumed saturation flow): agree = improves/better, worsens/worse or inconclusive/about unchanged

outcome.conclusion: [long-cycle] Known-answer test of the evaluation and selection stage (no proposer runs; Muse is not exercised). Positive control: the pre-registered correction I5 (greens {'EW': 15, 'NS': 10} s) was SELECTED; its Holm-confirmed improvements: mean_delay_s. Negative controls: the exact null I7 was rejected by the validator before simulation and not selected; the mirror I12 was simulated (compared) and not selected. Of 8 small perturbations of the bad plan (not nulls), 0 had a Holm-confirmed improvement and 4 worsened at least one metric. False positives (a confirmed improvement contradicting the pre-registered direction of an uncalibrated Webster model, which agreed with 50 of 99 predicted comparisons, 51%, and was opposite in 0): 0 of 7 confirmable claims predicted worse (rule-of-three 95% upper bound 0.43). In the baseline the queue was censored on arm N (vehicles held off at entry on seed 6), arm E (a lane filled on seeds 2, 8; vehicles held off at entry on seeds 1, 2, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 13, 16, 17), arm S (vehicles held off at entry on seeds 1, 2), arm W (vehicles held off at entry on seeds 4, 13, 19), so those arms' queue claims are untestable for every candidate (lower bounds).
